definitions.explanation: The floor directly above the ground level of a building. In a typical two-storey Japanese house, this is where bedrooms are usually located, with living areas on the first floor.

examples.japanese: {二階|にかい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{上|あ}がる→上がる：00615_agaru⟧。
⟦{寝室|しんしつ}→寝室：05300_shinshitsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{二階|にかい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
{二階|にかい}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{窓越|まどご}し⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{眺|なが}める→眺める：02132_nagameru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧だ。
examples.english: I like looking at the garden through the window from upstairs.

notes:
Formed with the counter ⟦{階|かい}→階：01034_kai⟧ (floors). Often used in expressions where "upstairs" would be natural in English, including the idiom below.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {二階|にかい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{上|あ}がる→上がる：00615_agaru⟧: to go up to the second floor
- {二階|にかい}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{降|お}りる→降りる：00568_oriru⟧: to come down from the second floor
- {二階|にかい}{建|だ}て: two-storey (building)
- {二階|にかい}⟦{席|せき}→席：02215_seki⟧: upper-deck seats (in a vehicle or theater)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {二階|にかい}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{目薬|めぐすり}→目薬：09714_megusuri⟧: "eye drops from the second floor" — doing something ineffective or roundabout (the medicine never reaches its target).

FORMS:
- ⟦{一階|いっかい}→一階：27512_ikkai⟧: first floor
- ⟦{三階|さんがい}→三階：27617_sangai⟧: third floor (note {連濁|れんだく}: かい → がい)
